subject: parameters estimates from non- Half-normal detection function

messages.author: 31e69dafd2f34e9e
messages.subject: parameters estimates from non- Half-normal detection function
parts:
Hello, everyone

I use the secr for my study species. The exponential detection function fit my data better than the half-normal function. I got the parameter estimates but I wonder that are the parameters derived from the half-normal distribution? If so, how robust it is to use those estimates inferences for non- Half-normal detection. How the different detection function influence the parameter estimates?


Thank you,
Ree

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: parameters estimates from non- Half-normal detection function
parts:
Hi Ree
The interpretation of the parameters labelled 'g0' and 'sigma' is specific to the particular shape of detection function that is fitted (e.g. halfnormal or negative exponential). In other words, we don't expect sigma-hat from the half normal to be the same as sigma-hat from the negative exponential - they relate to different parameters. This is certainly a potential trap. (One can compare the area of a circle enclosing, say, 95% of an equivalent 2-D activity distribution = home-range model, but that is getting rather technical and it is probably better done using lambda0 in the cumulative hazard parameterization (HHN, HEX). I'm not suggesting you do that, just indicating the possibility).
Murray
